title: The kill guard lets a session stop its own background job after the job is stranded under init
why: hooks/guard_kill.py checks ownership with `pid_is_owned` (descends from the session root), so it refuses a session's own job once stranded under init. `pid_is_session_job`, which wait-pid uses, also accepts a stranded job carrying this session's CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID. Hit: batch runner 10 could not stop its own batch 104 build (pid 27483).
source: batch runner 10, 10:11 CST Nov 12, via coordinator 10:12 CST; possible false alarm
note: Guard, code. Fix: the kill guard uses `pid_is_session_job`. Pairs with step stall-watch-ends-quiet-jobs. Ready, no lane.
